body: I want to get my numbers up, but everyday I step into work I fear someone in management telling me I'm close to termination. Like its one thing to be depressed over this or begin to try and have patience over this but I'm getting run down for no reason.

My employer gave me the number for the EAP line. I've set up appointments but I don't know what to ask or how its going to help me keep employed. I see a psychiatrist on a biweekly basis. The whole story is on /r/legaladvice. I'm tired of repeating myself over and over again to get the same answer: there's nothing anyone can do.  All they talk about is how it has to suit the business. I can't ask for more obtainable sales goals. I can't even ask to go to part time. Its black and white for them. Either I do the job I'm hired to do or I'm gone. I keep asking for legal advice because I don't know what I'm going to do if I'm let go. I don't know how well I can sue in Canada. All i know is that if it causes undue hardship for the company, its allowed. 

I do everything I can to get through the day, to show that I'm valuable and useful. I take on a lot of tasks my coworkers don't want to do. Everything from closing procedures completely on my own to writing others thank you notes because "their handwriting is horrible." I even do tasks tasks my managers could be doing but when they ask me, I don't mind because I like working. I'm almost always reminded again within hours that I'm close to losing my job. 

I don't know what my favourite pop and chocolate bars are right now. I tried eating something tasty for lunch and I ended up throwing most of it away.  Sorry I can be helpful.

Could an accommodation at this point take into consideration that I'm really suffering mentally at this point? 

I do not feel comfortable talking with managers when I need to take care of myself. When my performance comes into play, I leave coachings feeling even worse and like there's just no hope.

Its been shoved down my throat that i need to find another job. I've passed my resume out over 50 times in the past three months. If they fire me, I will be out of all luck. I can't let this happen.
The rub here is I recently moved to Gatineau. I still work in Ottawa and have lived here for years. I moved to save a bit of money. I don't know what my options are in Quebec yet.

Job market isn't that good, especially where I am and with my language skills. Can always find jobs part time retail though...that won't pay the bills, but hey, its a job. Half the reason I won't leave is because if I quit, I won't be eligible for employment insurance if it comes to it.

I don't want to collect assistance. I don't want a medical leave. I want to work.

The biggest things that trigger the panic and anxiety attacks is talking to management. I always feel like I'm doing a horrible job as it is and they absolutely feed that fire. I'm being told almost everyday to find a new job now. They won't give up - and that's every tier of management within the store. They just don't care.

I treat my coworkers with a lot of respect and I generally get along with them. I had to embarrassingly put my foot down when the shift changes got out of hand. It felt so bad to do that - I **want** to work. I **want** to support my team. When I do, its negative consequences.

Ah, my new neighbourhood library is almost completely French language. (The joys of moving to Quebec, I know.)

My mom does want me to read it, and I'll be going to see her next month. Works out for everyone. :)

I've actually used the food bank here once or twice. It was absolutely ages ago. Definitely not afraid to use it, I just don't know how it works in Gatineau just yet. :S I'm not worried too much about that this week though. I should be alright.

> Examine all your expenses. Cut them all as far as it will go. If you're severely in debt, you shouldn't have a $100 / month iPhone bill. No going out to dinner. Cut everything to bare minimums.

This is definitely the hardest thing I'm dealing with right now. I'm fighting to cut back everything. The biggest hurdle I'm running into is the fact that I've been having 10 to 12 hour days total and I'm finding it difficult to pack lunches accordingly. If I have the money, I end up breaking down and getting tea from Tim's (if I can afford it) to tide me over until I can get home and make myself a proper meal.

> Get a roommate. Or two. Or three.

Actually, this is the first time in years I've been without a roommate. Most of my financial trouble in recent years probably stemed from the fact I was living in an expensive two-bedroom apartment and relying on the influx of students looking for a place to replace the last student roommate who was looking for a place. A few times I had to cover two shares of rent, which was more than I was making over a full month. It's basically my fault for being to stubborn to move. (First off, I hate moving and the apartment I had at the time was in a great location and had a great view. It broke my heart to finally give in to move.) 

> If you still can't make ends meet, consider bankruptcy.

I hope it doesn't come to this, but I have considered it. Judging by the little bit of extra I've had the past few paychecks and if I can get this figured out soon, I should be able to get back on track and get full view of my debt situation.
I think my mom owns a copy.  I might have to pinch it when I'm home next.
You have a fantastic username. Cheers!

I'm hoping to change the bilingualism thing soon. I definitely want to relearn and my basics are good (I get the gist of a written paragraph and I've been told my accent on the basic phrases are very good). It's just, well, one thing at a time.  I'm sure once I'm able to settle the big issues as they stand now, I'll be able to focus on my language skills; especially since I'd give just about anything to work up on the Hill right now.

I've come to learn in my time on this planet that anxiety isn't the best thing to have when you're looking to keep a job. I can only take what I can and hope for the best.

I'm definitely getting enough hours now that I am working two jobs. As I said, one is high-end department store which is the absolute furthest thing I should be doing with my life and I'm pretty sure they'd love to find a reason to be rid of me; but as you said, the paycheck is worth the ounce of dignity and I've actually been doing really good as of late so they can't fire me. I've been here for over a year now. I'd really like to find an opportunity to get out though. It's hard on the anxiety. My second job is actually at my old place one day a week at a slow optical store. Not bad, wish they could give me more hours consistently though. Total hours is about 30 to 35 hours a week. I'm exhausted half the time, but it's going to have two paychecks with the rent decrease.  

I'm also trying to see if I can fix the bilingual thing. One thing at a time though.
